name: Question 18
problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point $C(1,4,-14)$ and is parallel to the two distinct lines $r=⟨-1,5,7⟩+s⟨1,1,1⟩$ and $r=⟨0,3,-19⟩+t⟨-2,-2,-2⟩.$
worked_solution:
The direction vectors of the lines are ${v}_{1}=⟨-2,-2,-2⟩$ and ${v}_{2}=⟨1,1,1⟩,$ respectively.
But ${v}_{2}=-2{v}_{1}.$ So, our lines are parallel. 

Despite this fact, two distinct parallel lines still determine a plane. Now: 

- from the equation of the first line, we get the point $P$ with the position vector $p=⟨-1,5,7⟩$ that lies on it, and

- from the equation of the second line, we get the point $Q$ with the position vector $q=⟨0,3,-19⟩$ that lies on it.

The vector $u=q-p$ will be parallel to the required plane. 

Computing the coordinates of $u,$  we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =q-p \\  & =⟨0,3,-19⟩-⟨-1,5,7⟩ \\  & =⟨1,-2,-26⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since $\overset{\to }{PQ}∦{v}_{1},$ we can find the equation of our plane.

We know that the point $C(1,4,-14)$ lies on the plane and its position vector is $c=⟨1,4,-14⟩.$  

So, the corresponding parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =c+s{v}_{1}+tu \\ r & =⟨1,4,-14⟩+s⟨1,1,1⟩+t⟨1,-2,-26⟩,\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 18
?

Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point C(1,4,−14) and is parallel to the two distinct lines r=⟨−1,5,7⟩+s⟨1,1,1⟩ and r=⟨0,3,−19⟩+t⟨−2,−2,−2⟩.

a
r=⟨−2,−2,−2⟩+s⟨1,4,−14⟩+t⟨1,1,1⟩,s,t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=⟨1,4,−14⟩+s⟨−2,−2,−2⟩+t⟨1,1,1⟩,s,t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=⟨0,3,−19⟩+s⟨−2,−2,−2⟩+t⟨1,2,3⟩,s,t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=⟨1,4,−14⟩+s⟨1,1,1⟩+t⟨1,−2,−26⟩,s,t∈(−∞,∞)
e
The plane is undefined
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The direction vectors of the lines are v1=⟨−2,−2,−2⟩ and v2=⟨1,1,1⟩, respectively. But v2=−2v1. So, our lines are parallel.

Despite this fact, two distinct parallel lines still determine a plane. Now:

  • from the equation of the first line, we get the point P with the position vector p=⟨−1,5,7⟩ that lies on it, and

  • from the equation of the second line, we get the point Q with the position vector q=⟨0,3,−19⟩ that lies on it.

The vector u=q−p will be parallel to the required plane.

Computing the coordinates of u, we obtain

u=q−p=⟨0,3,−19⟩−⟨−1,5,7⟩=⟨1,−2,−26⟩

Finally, since PQ→∦v1, we can find the equation of our plane.

We know that the point C(1,4,−14) lies on the plane and its position vector is c=⟨1,4,−14⟩.

So, the corresponding parametric equation of the plane is given by

r=c+sv1+tur=⟨1,4,−14⟩+s⟨1,1,1⟩+t⟨1,−2,−26⟩,s,t∈(−∞,∞).
